texts.preamble: Sumit vs . Vinod & Ors. on 10 November, 2022 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 30/18 Fir no. 425/17 U/s 279/338 Ipc Ps Oia Cnr No.: Dlse01-009125-2017 Sumit Vs. No. B-431, Dakshinpuri, New Delhi. ............Driver/Respondent no. 2. Satish Arora S/o Sh. Baldev Raj R/o H. No. 43/3rd Floor Gali no.1, Govindpuri, Kalkaji New Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 3. Chola Mandalam Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. Mact No. 30/18 Sumit Vs. Vinod & Ors. Page No. 1 of 22 rpt Karol Bagh, New Delhi. .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Date of accident : 02.11.2017 Date of filing of Dar : 05.12.2017 Date of Decision : 10.11.2022 Sumit vs . texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179135124/ 1 Award 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 05.12.2017 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the facts of the case, on 02.11.2017 at about 12.30 pm, injured/ victim was going to his school and was waiting bus near Maa Anandmai Marg, Indira Kalyan Vihar, bus stop. Suddenly, the offending vehicle bearing no. DL 1VB 9237 stopped at the said bus stop and when the minor injured was trying to board, the driver of the said vehicle ran the bus in very fast speed without following the traffic rules due to which the injured fell down on the road and sustained injury. The injured was taken to ESI Hospital by driver of the offending vehicle, where his MLC no. 503/17 was prepared and thereafter, he was removed to Safdarjang Hospital. 3. Accordingly the FIR in question was registered and altimately charge sheet u/s 279/338 IPC was filed. 4. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 15.12.2018 noticing 62% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb. 5. Further, as per record, no reply filed by R-1 & 2. 6. Legal offer is filed by insurance company but the same is not accepted MACT No. 30/18 Sumit Vs. Vinod & Ors. Page No. 2 of 22 rpt by the petitioner. Hence, the matter proceeded further on merit. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal : 1. Whether the petitioner received injuries in the accident which took place on 02.11.2017 at about 12.30 PM involving offending vehicle i.e. bearing no. DL 1VB 9237 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1/ driver, owned by R-2/owner and insured with R-3/Insurance Company R3? OPP. 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 9. As per record, PW-1 Sh. Ram Vilash (father of minor victim/ injured) examined himself and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/A to Ex. PW-1/H. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. Sumit vs . Vinod & Ors. on 10 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179135124/ 2 10. Injured /Minor, Master Sumit Kumar also examined as PW-2 in the court itself in his examination in chief. He was also cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. 11. Further, as per record, None of the respondent led any evidence. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 18. During cross examination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company, PW-2 MACT No. 30/18 Sumit Vs. Vinod & Ors. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 21.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 24. In Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as "M. R. Krishna Murthi vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. on 5 March, 2019, (2020) 15 SCC 493: (2020) 4 SCC (Crl.) 84: 2019 SCC Online SC 315 , after dealing with various case laws relating to injury matters and death cases in case of students, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: "24. In those cases where the victim of the accident is not an earning person but a student, while assessing the compensation for loss of future earning, the focus of the examination would be the career prospect and the likely earning of such a person in future. It is further argued that grievous injury, if any and disability alleged is due to some other independent cause and not due to such accident. It is further argued that there is no functional disability in any case. 33. On the other hand, it is argued by learned counsel for petitioner that at least there is 62% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb. It is further argued that victim/ injured was minor of a tender age of 14 years only MACT No. 30/18 Sumit Vs. Vinod & Ors. Page No. 11 of 22 rpt and due to such disability suffered at such young age, his whole future and normal life is spoiled. It is further claimed that as such, functional disability of 62 % in relation to whole body be given in the present case. 41. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: MACT No. 30/18 Sumit Vs. Vinod & Ors. Page No. 16 of 22 rpt "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
